answer: An agent marketplace requires each voting identity to lock 100 credits in escrow for 30 days, and the same credits cannot back two identities. Agents named jade, shale, and mesa each meet that requirement. An attacker creating 1,000 fake agents must therefore immobilize 100,000 credits to gain their votes, sacrificing liquidity and potential returns elsewhere. Splitting one funded identity into many names creates no extra voting power.
